I think the point is in the middle, like most things. 
The current situation is a lot more appreciable than before, but it still has some things to improve. Mainly the previous shortcomings of some units are more evident because old A5 was entirely stat checkable with just investment for the most part.
The new difficulty made so people can't force clear stages with favorites anymore, but this is not just a problem with enemy scaling but with the units themselves too. They need to study their performances and see how to improve them when needed, but the problem is that it seems they will be doing that only in 2.7, so there will be some time in witch some will continue to be less performing than others. 
For the highest tiers, there is also the dissonance with the expectation that one can use a favorite in any stage if they are on max investment like before, but for the direct objective to keep Morimens challenging, now the very max difficulty is normally only doable with a maxed team that is also good in the wave, like a normal dtide stage. This could be also smoothed over a bit with the balance pass, but if the endgame point is to always be challenging no mater the investment, as for the core of the game, that will probably not change completely.

in my opinion powercreep in gachas are inevitable but controllable. 

linear and steady inflation is acceptable, but exponential inflation is just a big mistake. game balance is thrown off course, you end up needing to buff more units, and more units will be “left out” in the gutter 

as for the state of dtide, triangle difficulty to me is just a huge waste of time with turn rewinds and DR triggers. I don’t see the appeal on spending anywhere from 1~5 hours on a single wave even though i could. 

i had more enjoyment playing different and creating new teams for alert 5 that didn’t require such huge investment and time needed to clear one wave
